expectations.text: Lists the all-hazards, 10-measure minimum set — policies on risk analysis, incident handling, business continuity/backup/DR/crisis management, supply chain security, secure development/vulnerability handling, effectiveness testing, cyber hygiene/training, cryptography policies, HR/access control/asset management, and MFA/secured communications
expectations.evidence: Lists all ten Art. 21(2)(a)-(j) measures: risk analysis policies, incident handling, business continuity/backup/DR/crisis management, supply chain, secure acquisition/development, effectiveness assessment, hygiene/training, cryptography, HR/access/asset management, MFA/secured communications

expectations.text: Emphasises supply chain security including direct supplier relationships as an explicit measure
expectations.evidence: (d) Supply chain security. A register of critical ICT suppliers, pre-onboarding security assessments, contractual security obligations

expectations.text: Notes proportionality: measures appropriate to the risks, entity size, and societal impact
expectations.evidence: Proportionality is assessed against your size, risk exposure, likelihood/severity of incidents, and cost of implementation

expectations.text: Mentions the effectiveness-assessment obligation (policies and procedures to assess whether measures work)
expectations.evidence: (f) Effectiveness assessment. KPIs/KRIs per measure... at least annual internal audits or management reviews

expectations.text: Frames ISO 27001 correctly if raised: strong implementation vehicle but not a safe harbor (registration, reporting timelines, governance duties sit outside certification)
expectations.evidence: certification is not a safe harbor: it does not by itself satisfy the Art. 23 reporting timelines, the Art. 20 personal-accountability and training obligations, Art. 27 registration
